description.value: The study examined whether fMRI BOLD responses to cocaine cues predict treatment effectiveness and relapse in cocaine-dependent patients.

spans.text: In the current pilot study, we examined the potential of brain activity changes in response to cocaine cues to predict relapse to cocaine use as assessed using the Treatment Effectiveness Score (TES)

value: We hypothesized that, during the first 30 s of viewing of cocaine cues by treatment-seeking CD subjects, activation of brain regions previously implicated in cocaine craving, including areas of frontal and anterior and posterior cingulate cortices, would be inversely associated with TES scores and related to relapse.
Specifically, we predicted that individuals with TES scores below the mean TES score would show more activation in these brain regions.

value: The BOLD response to the first 30 s of tape viewing compared to the baseline response showed five clusters that had significant positive correlations with the TES (r = 0.64; P < 0.005). The largest areas of activation were the right lingual and left posterior cingulate cortices; the right superior temporal and right inferior occipital cortices also were associated with the TES. No negative correlations were found between the TES and brain activation.
